## Goal

Make supported TreeDB typed-row reads and indexed durable mutations substantially cheaper through a coherent collection execution architecture, with bounded publication/reclamation work and representative public-path evidence. This is the **performance successor** to closed [#5056](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5056), whose finite capability/correctness qualification remains accepted.

Recommended design: a shared snapshot-bound row executor and direct owned output; source-aware native update plans that retain unchanged physical fields; bounded identity-free preparation with one authoritative ordered commit; resumable immutable-manifest retirement with short validated fences. Reuse existing COW/publication, command-WAL prefix and resource authority rather than add competing engines.

The user requested architectural redesign tickets on 2026-10-06 Honolulu. The subsequent user request to execute this graph with codex-issue-graph-executor authorizes focused implementation and merge after the required gates. Execution is recorded in the durable state comment.

## Evidence and its limits

Source preflight: live main `b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a` on 2026-10-07 UTC. Production TreeDB runtime has no delta from measured `3325dfe77940fec8587d8b61b1ac4e0b2f72caca`; intervening TreeDB changes are tests/docs, and later matched-maintenance tooling changed separately. These are historical frozen measurements, **not a fresh benchmark of main**. [Accepted report](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/d941fb6222bc1ea2c8d766756674c40c7dd8ed8c/TreeDB/docs/evidence/r1-row-store-5061/README.md).

| --- | --- | --- |

| Typed prepared batch / prepared range / ordinary range | 138.816 µs/32 rows; 48.619 µs/10 rows; 118.762 µs/10 rows | Reuse improves some routes; public ordinary costs remain different. |

| Finite D lifecycle | 4,096 live rows, 512 hot IDs; active vlog 193,991 → 445,187 B | Active append retention is real; five epochs do not establish a scale bound. |
| Immutable manifest GC | Full directory revalidated for each 16-deletion batch; locks span the whole call | Confirmed O(N²/16) worst-case scans; descriptor bound is not a pause/work bound. |

Read timings compare complete equivalent outputs only within each route. Historical prepared-range timing composes ordinary index IDs with a held fetch view under quiescence; it is not one captured concurrent index/fetch operation. The ordinary public complete range is the coherent route. The C callback returns a pre-encoded replacement and does not decode the old row; planner reconstruction remains charged. Prepared setup/first fetch is separate. Point Get and wide-update timing groups were inconclusive. Whole-process Go allocations and fixture/oracle-retained heap are not DB-only/RSS measures; SQLite C allocations are excluded. Historical costs accepted under #5056 are inputs to this reprioritized performance work, not retroactive failures of that completed graph.

## Current architecture and reuse/removal decisions

- [GetInto](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/api.go#L22680) reconstructs into another owned buffer before its final append into caller storage. Point, ordinary range and prepared fetch already have coherent snapshot/materializer semantics; consolidate their executor and scratch ownership, not snapshot correctness from scratch.
- Current catalog metadata is immutable/shared. The row reader already has a shared verified 64 MiB offset memo; a new cache is unwarranted. The separate per-view pointRowBlocks map can retain decoded blocks without a bound, and held offsets sit outside the global memo cap; reader lifetime budgets must cover these owners. Classic manifests and cold assets can require full inventory/validation; source-directory V2 already supplies a point-local route. Select a strategy explicitly rather than call all formats equivalent.
- [Update planning](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/api.go#L19224) reconstructs old complete rows for generic callbacks. Native replace shares the planner and avoids part of that work; [metadata updates](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/typed_metadata.go#L296) already preserve physical coordinates. Reuse these plans, index validation and publisher.
- [Prepared inserts](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/prepared_insert.go#L362) are single-use, owned and identity-free, but currently unindexed semantic-stream JSON and require sealed-root completion. They are a design seam, not a drop-in R1 native updater.
- [Typed upsert grouping](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/collections/typed_upsert_group.go#L49) and backend durable-prefix groups already exist, with bounded insert-only/no-unique eligibility. Generic typed updates are not automatically admitted. Extend selected existing admission only if [#5091](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5091) proves its value.
- [Manifest revision GC](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/b21d017758b167aecc23a4d1afc7fb8148d09d7a/TreeDB/db/leaf_manifest_revision_gc.go#L21) has bounded handles but quadratic rescans/whole-call writer and snapshot locks. [#5095](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5095) owns that specific architectural residual.
- Visible/candidate/seal closure cloning exists in `root_publication_activation.go` at 202/548/1046; it does not yet explain the checkpoint allocation increase. [#5091](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5091) assigns the measured residual before implementation: existing #5015/#5016 if shared closure work owns it, a new collection packet if its intermediates own it, or a narrowly scoped publication-memory child only if a distinct cause is demonstrated. An unassigned blocking cost prevents completion.

## North-star gates and metric classes

| Gate / class | Pass evidence | Failure action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public read cost/scaling — north star | Repeatable material improvement on complete point GetInto and ordinary bounded ranges against matched baseline; no repeated full-manifest/asset preparation per returned row on the selected eligible strategy; ownership/setup costs charged | Revise read architecture; keep gate open |
| Native indexed mutation cost — north star | Selected bio/email/city updates avoid old full-document reconstruction and unchanged typed-field rewriting; materially lower processing/allocations than equivalent whole-row callback updates; report complete durable request latency separately | Fix plan or mapped limiter; do not substitute relaxed ACK |
| Ordered execution — exit gate, conditional C mechanism | Finite owned-byte/queue admission, one authoritative commit sequence and complete atomic index effects; activated preparation/grouping improves its declared metric | Remove rejected mechanism, map remaining product obligation |
| Publication memory — north star | Explain checkpoint allocation increase with exclusive attribution; eliminate avoidable amplification through its sole owner, or explicitly accept a minimized required budget with measured alternatives | Assign/revise residual owner; no unowned or unexplained gap |
| Reclamation economics — north star | Lower scan complexity and bounded per-step work/fence duration; held-reader/recovery-safe deletion; storage trajectories explain active files and debt through representative churn/rollover | Fix retirement or map an exclusive active-retention owner |
| Correctness/durability/ownership — guardrail | Full rows, current and historical postings, batch conflicts/no-ops, held views, reopen/process cuts and affected modeled power-loss tests pass | Block merge/qualification |
| Allocation/residency/I/O/storage — guardrail | Comparable B/op/objects plus live/peak heap/RSS where supported, sync counts, WAL-excluded durable bytes/debt; explain and minimize material tradeoffs | Block unexplained regression |
| SQLite timings, Dgraph/hybrid/vector results — observational/shared guardrails | Same semantics for any comparison; existing consumers protected | No universal ranking or unrelated hard-goal claim |

[#5091](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5091) freezes quantitative budgets from attributable stable controls, workload sizes, repetitions and noise before candidates. Qualitative structural gates above are already fixed. Targets may be revised only by a consequential documented decision; a failed experiment or linked follow-up does not close an unmet north-star gate. A genuinely unavoidable I/O cost requires measured lower-bound evidence and explicit acceptance of a narrower endpoint, reported separately from the original performance goal.

## Test, documentation and retained evidence policy


## Semantic and performance contract

Preserve complete logical rows, residual JSON null/missing semantics, stable ascending bounded ranges, pending-write/tombstone visibility, one captured publication for index selection plus fetch, owned results after view close, and borrowed callback lifetime limits. Preserve batch atomic primary/secondary state, unique final-owner validation, no-op and missing-ID counts, deterministic canonical command replay, pre-append refusal and post-durable ambiguity/poison/reopen behavior. Ordinary command-WAL durable ACK and prepared-insert sealed-root completion are distinct; do not copy the stronger prepared-insert boundary onto unrelated APIs or weaken ordinary ACKs.

The value log is persistent storage. Both recoverable durable metas, queued/visible roots, snapshots and exact resource pins govern reclamation. File and directory durability, stable identity/frontier validation and stale-plan rejection remain authoritative. A scheduling cache, filename, age or digest alone grants no deletion authority. Pre-alpha format changes are allowed when selected, with explicit rebuild/version refusal, storage/recovery docs and tests; no migration subsystem by default.

Every runtime packet owns its affected specs, verification entries and practical guide changes in the implementing PR. Trace and extend existing optimized paths; consolidate obsolete routes/options/helpers only after consumer and invariant proof. Do not create a second catalog/row-offset cache, transaction engine, command WAL, durability profile or GC authority.


Each owning PR starts with a public invariant/contract test or explicit refactor characterization, implements its complete feature with allocation minimization and docs, then runs focused/affected races/recovery and matched performance. Read/mutation/commit/reclamation are performance-objective; harness/schema is performance-sensitive instrumentation with validator rejection tests and no runtime speedup claim; artifact-only report work is not runtime-performance-relevant.

Retained order is product → reviewed/landed [#5096](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5096) → exact source/harness/binary freeze → [#5097](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5097) artifacts. Use a high-capacity Linux runner, persistent build cache and durable artifacts after verifying availability; otherwise record `INFRASTRUCTURE_UNAVAILABLE: runner|cache|storage: reason` and actual fallback. Shared hosts are allowed with recorded activity and interleaved controls; absolute quiet is not required. Preserve noisy/failed attempts and invalidate only evidence affected by runtime/harness drift. Mature exact-head review and CI gates remain required.

Reassess after [#5091](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5091), first read/native-mutation slice, and representative publication/reclamation evidence. Record changed assumptions, revise bodies/edges, preserve useful merged work and one owner per obligation. Do not reopen a measurement campaign merely because unrelated main moves.
